mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and lower corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 2% for three months indicates a high-inflation, high-rate regime, which erodes real corporate earnings and compresses valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: high inflation and high interest rate regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and S&P 500 returns over the prior 12 months signals a regime where consumer spending boosts earnings, and this relationship persists to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation between PAYEMS growth and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns in the next out-of-sample period.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent fall in both UNRATE and PAYEMS (below their 12-month moving averages) for two consecutive months signals a dual deterioration in labor market participation and employment, which reduces aggregate demand and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both below 12-month moving average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE and PAYEMS are below their 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% in a single month signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average +10% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST jumps above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% in a single month.
